gap: No result ChatGPT got states an independently measured noise, distortion or jitter figure for any candidate: Hi-Fi News measured the Denon DCD-600 at 95.3 dB A-weighted S/N, 0.0013% THD and 480 psec jitter, and an Audio Science Review member measured the Yamaha CD-S303 at 95.7 dB dynamic range, 0.0022% THD+N and 1.74 V output.
standout_why: insideouthomereviews.com (read 2026-11-08) compares the CD-S303, DCD-600NE and NAD C 538 only on maker specs and says so ('Specs come from each manufacturer's own pages, manuals and data sheets'); the Yamaha, Onkyo and Denon spec/manual pages and the Crutchfield/B&H compare pages ChatGPT got carry only the makers' claimed 105 dB / 107 dB / 110 dB S/N figures. None cites a lab measurement. Crutchfield compare pages returned 403 and could not be read.
decides: It confirms rather than overturns the pick: both of the two most-cited budget players measure to roughly the same 95 dB noise floor, well below the makers' 105 dB (Yamaha) and 110 dB (Denon) claims, so neither has a measurable sound-quality edge and the choice can rest on price, outputs and features. Two usable details: the Denon's 1.92 Vrms output is near the 2 V standard while the Yamaha's 1.74 Vrms sits 1.2 dB low (the Yamaha will sound quieter at the same volume setting), and the Yamaha was verified bit-perfect as a transport over optical, which matters for anyone feeding an external DAC. No independent measurement exists for the Onkyo C-7030, so its 107 dB claim stays unverified.

findings.label: Digital filter stopband attenuation
findings.source_title: Yamaha CD-S303 Review (CD Player) - Audio Science Review forum
findings.note: Channel imbalance -0.1 dB across the band; noise rise above 25 kHz. Intersample-over test: filter has more than 1 dB of headroom (5512.5 Hz at +0.69 dBFS stays noise-dominated at -65.8 dB).
